title: Building Blocks for LLM Systems & Products: Eugene Yan
talk_summary: Eugene Yan lays out four reusable patterns for LLM products: automated evals as the foundation, retrieval-augmented generation with attention to document position and irrelevance thresholds, guardrails for factual consistency, and implicit-feedback collection. The core message is to start evals small (30-100 examples), simplify tasks to deterministic checks where possible, and reuse classic IR/recommendation techniques rather than reinventing them.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build a small, domain-specific eval set per task and run it automatically on every prompt/retrieval/model change instead of relying on academic benchmarks or eyeballing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: he starts with an eval set of 40 questions for his domain expert Tas 40 evils that's all it takes
takeaways.numbers: 40-question eval set cited as sufficient to start

takeaways.technique: Deterministic checks over LLM judges where possible
takeaways.what_they_do: Simplify the task so it can be scored deterministically: run generated SQL and compare results, validate extracted JSON keys/values, use precision/recall for classification-like tasks, reserving LLM judges for open-ended output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can try to run the SQL and see if it Returns the expected result that's very deterministic

takeaways.technique: Rank retrieved context highly; position matters
takeaways.what_they_do: Even with large context windows, put the most relevant documents first; accuracy drops when the answer sits mid-context, sometimes below no-retrieval baseline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it's somewhere in the middle it's actually worse accuracy than having no retrieval the generation
takeaways.numbers: Answer in first doc = highest accuracy; mid-context worse than no retrieval; top-position accuracy only ~75%

takeaways.what_they_do: LLMs are tuned to be helpful and will answer even when retrieved context is irrelevant; add a similarity/distance threshold to skip the LLM step when nothing is relevant.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I think it helps to include a threshold to exclude irrelevant documents

takeaways.technique: NLI-style factual consistency at sentence granularity
takeaways.what_they_do: Use natural language inference (premise=source, hypothesis=claim) to detect hallucinations, applied per-sentence rather than per-document for finer detection.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as we got finer and finer from document to paragraph to sentence the accuracy of detecting factual inconsistency goes up

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument product UX so organic user actions (accept/reject suggestion, rerun, upscale) become labeled feedback, building a data flywheel without asking users.
takeaways.evidence_quote: rerunning the prompt is negative reward where the user doesn't like any of the images
